Zero Speed Switch Sensor and Target Selection

A zero speed switch sensor is the non contact pickup that faces a rotating target on the shaft and sends one pulse each time a target passes. The controller compares the pulse period with the underspeed setpoint, so the sensor and target choice decides how reliable the trip is. Most units use an inductive sensor with steel targets, while some use a Hall effect element with a magnet.

ItemInductive sensorHall effect sensor
TargetHigh iron bolt heads, toothed disc or slotted collarMagnet fixed on the shaft or disc
Sensing gapSmall, for example 1/16 to 1/8 inch on bolt headsLarger gap than a plain steel target
Target material limitsStainless steel and some iron alloys may not trigger itNeeds a magnet, steel grade does not matter
Mounting pointTail, boot or non driven shaftTail, boot or non driven shaft
Common faultGap too wide or wrong target metalMagnet loose or missing

Space the targets evenly so the pulse period stays steady at constant speed, and keep the sensor on the non driven pulley. If the belt slips on the drive pulley, only the non driven shaft slows down, so a sensor placed there sees the real belt movement and trips the drive in time.
